title: AI helpdesk: replacing the old help desk in 2026 | Keloa
text:
An AI helpdesk is not Zendesk with a plugin. It is a help desk where the AI is the first responder by default, the operator inbox is built for escalations, and the pricing is based on AI reply volume instead of how many people log in. The shift is bigger than it looks from a feature checklist.

60-70% Tickets typically auto-resolved

€0 Extra per operator seat: seats are included

EU Hosting, GDPR-first by design

TL;DR

An AI helpdesk puts the AI agent first, the operator inbox second, and aligns pricing with AI reply volume. It replaces traditional per-seat help desks for teams that want the AI to handle the bulk of tickets and humans to handle the escalations with full context.

- ✓ AI is the default first responder. Humans are the second-line, with summary and citations already attached.
- ✓ Per-reply pricing, not per-seat. Add operators without adding costs.
- ✓ The inbox is built around escalations, not raw ticket queues. The AI did the easy work already.
- ✓ Knowledge base, AI agent, and inbox in one place. No three-tool stack with broken sync.

...

Most migrations are simpler than vendors will lead you to believe. The pieces that matter: forward the support email address, drop the new chat widget on the site, and import your old knowledge base if you have one. Conversation history is rarely worth the migration headache, the new AI helpdesk starts fresh and your customers do not care which system held their refund question from two years ago. Plan a quiet weekend, run both inboxes for a week, then turn the old one off.

## Where Keloa fits

Keloa is built as an AI helpdesk from the ground up. AI agent first, operator inbox second, knowledge base on the side, all in one product. Seven channels are live today: chat widget, email, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, Telegram and Slack, and the AI agent answers end to end on each. There is one package with everything included, priced to your AI reply volume from €49 a month. Hosted in the EU, with a free Verwerkersovereenkomst (DPA) and one-click data export if you ever want to leave.

...

Yes. You forward your existing support inbox (support@yourbrand.com or whatever you use) to your Keloa address, or you set up a separate Keloa email channel for support. Replies go out from your address, not from a Keloa subdomain, because the customer should never see the back-end change.

...

No. The fastest adopters in 2026 are e-commerce brands, B2B SaaS, financial services, and direct-to-consumer goods. The pattern is the same everywhere: a high volume of repetitive questions sits underneath a smaller pile of complex ones. The AI handles the volume.

## EU-hosted is not the same as EU-owned.

Most of these tools, Replyful included, run on servers in the EU that belong to US cloud providers. That is normal, and a DPA with standard contractual clauses covers it. What differs is everything around the database. Ask any vendor these five things.

1. 01

### Where is the company, and who can be compelled to hand over data?

A US company, or a European one owned by a US parent, can receive US legal orders even for data stored in Frankfurt. A European company on a US cloud is one step removed. Only self-hosting on your own servers takes the question off the table.
2. 02

### Is EU storage the default, or a plan you have to buy?

Some tools keep every account in the EU. Others offer it only on higher plans, as an add-on, or by request when the account is created. Moving an existing account later can mean a migration.
3. 03

### Where does the AI run?

Tickets stored in the EU can still be sent to a model in the US for every AI reply or summary. Ask where inference happens and whether the provider can train on your data.
4. 04

### Who are the sub-processors?

Email delivery, attachments, search, analytics and sign-in are often separate companies. A public sub-processor list shows which ones see conversation content and where they are.
5. 05

### Where are backups and logs kept, and for how long?

A database in the EU with backups or error logs elsewhere is not EU-hosted. Ask for the backup location and the retention window after you delete data.

...

Of the tools compared here, Crisp, Dixa, Replyful and Trengo are European companies that store data in the EU. Freshdesk, Deskpro and Zendesk are US companies with an EU region: Freshdesk on any plan if chosen at signup, Deskpro on request, and Zendesk from Suite Professional with its Data Center Location add-on.

Is an EU-hosted helpdesk enough for GDPR?

No tool makes you GDPR compliant on its own. EU hosting removes the need for transfer safeguards for the stored data, but you still need a DPA with the vendor, a lawful basis, retention rules and a way to answer access and deletion requests. Check where the AI runs and who the sub-processors are, too.
